guide.collab_warning.body: This tour will draw on the canvas, and everyone in the room will see it. Local removal later will not remove it for them.
guide.collab_warning.title: You're in a shared room
guide.completed.body: That's the end of this one. Everything you made is yours to keep.
guide.completed.title: Done
guide.deck.rejected: These story steps could not be read. Nothing is wrong with your story — ask whoever sent the link to send it again.
guide.demo_prompt.body: This tour added a panel to your story. You can keep it and carry on, or remove it now.
guide.demo_prompt.title: Keep what the tour drew?
guide.failed.body: Something it needs isn't available right now. Nothing you did caused this, and your work is untouched.
guide.failed.title: This tour can't continue
guide.library.broken: The tour catalog could not be read. Nothing is wrong with your story — try reopening the guide.
guide.library.title: Guides
guide.unavailable.body: It needs something this editor doesn't have right now — a tool that isn't unlocked yet, or more room on screen.
guide.unavailable.title: This tour isn't available here
tour.collab.drawing.description: How a shared canvas works when someone else is drawing with you.
tour.collab.drawing.step.done.body: You draw, they draw, both screens stay in step. Everything you made during this tour is yours to keep.
tour.collab.drawing.step.done.title: That's the whole idea
tour.collab.drawing.step.intro.body: When you share a room, you and the other person draw on the same story. Everything either of you adds shows up on both screens. This tour walks through it once, at your pace.
tour.collab.drawing.step.intro.title: Drawing together
tour.collab.drawing.step.same-story.body: Tap {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} to line your panels up in a row. Ask the other person to tap it too: each screen decides where its own panels sit, so running it on both is what lines your stories up.
tour.collab.drawing.step.their-turn.body: Ask them to draw something too. This step continues on its own the moment their work reaches you.
tour.collab.drawing.step.their-turn.fall: Their drawing hasn't come through. They may still be getting settled — you can carry on and it will appear whenever they draw.
tour.collab.drawing.step.wait-peer.body: Share your room link or code, and this step continues by itself as soon as they arrive. Nothing is lost while you wait.
tour.collab.drawing.step.wait-peer.fallb: Nobody joined yet. You can keep going through the tour and invite someone later — the room stays open.
tour.collab.drawing.step.wait-peer.title: Waiting for someone to join
tour.collab.drawing.step.who-drew-what.b:
Tap {icon:cmd:layers_panel_toggle} to open the layers panel.

Each person's work gets its own layer there, labelled with their name. Yours stay yours — you can hide or change your own layers without touching theirs.
tour.collab.drawing.step.who-is-here.bod:
Tap the collaboration button to open the panel.

It lists everyone here, and the crown marks whoever opened the room. It closes whenever you tap the canvas — that's normal, and this button brings it back.
tour.collab.drawing.step.who-is-here.fal: This tour needs a shared room. Open one from the start screen, then come back to it.
tour.collab.drawing.step.your-turn.body: Draw a stroke inside this first panel. The other person sees it appear on their screen as soon as you lift your finger.
tour.collab.drawing.step.your-turn.title: {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} Draw something
tour.collab.drawing.title: Drawing together
tour.collab.drawing.unavailableHint: Drawing together is switched off in this browser. Open {icon:gear} Settings → Collab Drawing and turn on **Enable Collab Drawing**, then come back — {icon:collab} will appear at the top right, and nothing here is missing from the app itself.
tour.demo.placement.description: Internal: exercises collision-aware placement against real UI.
tour.demo.placement.step.authored-prefer: This step asks for the top-left corner and gets it, because nothing is in the way.
tour.demo.placement.step.bottom-right-ta: The panel has to move out of the way of the control this step points at.
tour.demo.placement.step.protected-centr: This step protects the middle of the screen even though it highlights nothing.
tour.demo.placement.step.top-left-target: Now the highlight is somewhere else, and the panel follows the nearest free spot.
tour.demo.placement.title: Panel placement
tour.demo.stage0.step.collab-button.body: Tap the collaboration button to open the panel, where you can invite someone to draw with you.
tour.demo.stage0.step.first-frame.body: This is the first panel of your story. Tap it to start drawing.
tour.demo.stage0.step.first-frame.title: {icon:cmd:add_frame} Your first panel
tour.demo.stage0.step.welcome.body: This short tour highlights a few things worth knowing. Use Next to move on, or close any time.
tour.demo.stage0.step.welcome.title: {icon:drawing-tools} Welcome
tour.demo.stage0.title: Quick tour
tour.demo.stage1.step.draw-something.bod: With {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} active, draw a quick stroke in the first panel.
tour.demo.stage1.step.move-frame.body: With {icon:cmd:editor_move_mode_toggle} on, drag inside the first panel to move what's drawn there.
tour.demo.stage1.step.move-frame.title: {icon:cmd:editor_move_mode_toggle} Move it around
tour.demo.stage1.step.toggle-draw.body: Tap {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} to leave move mode and start drawing again.
tour.demo.stage1.step.toggle-draw.title: {icon:cmd:editor_move_mode_toggle} {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} Turn drawing back on
tour.demo.stage1.step.toggle-move.body: Tap {icon:cmd:editor_move_mode_toggle} to turn move mode on.
tour.demo.stage1.step.toggle-move.title: {icon:cmd:editor_move_mode_toggle} Move mode
tour.demo.stage1.title: Try it yourself
tour.demo.stage2.description: A tour that prepares a scene for you.
tour.demo.stage2.step.look-at-it.body: This panel was added just for this tour, so you have something to experiment with right away.
tour.demo.stage2.step.look-at-it.title: {icon:cmd:add_frame} We drew this for you
tour.demo.stage2.title: See it in action
tour.handbook.stage1.description: Create, select, reorder and clone the panels your story is made of.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.add-first-fram:
Tap {icon:cmd:add_frame} on the top toolbar.

A drawing frame appears on the screen — an empty panel of your story.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.add-more-frame: Tap {icon:cmd:add_frame} twice more. A story needs somewhere to go.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.clone-frame.bo:
With a frame selected, tap {icon:cmd:clone_selected_frame} on the top toolbar.

A duplicate appears beside the original — useful when the next panel is a small change from this one.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.deleting.body:
{icon:cmd:delete_selected_frame_content} on the top toolbar deletes the **selected frame** — the frame itself and everything drawn in it.

Tap it now. It asks first: the button turns into a warning, and a **second tap confirms**. Tapping anywhere else cancels.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.deleting.title: {icon:cmd:delete_selected_frame_content} Deleting
tour.handbook.stage1.step.done.body:
You can create frames, select them, clone them and put them in order.

Next: drawing in them.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.done.title: Stage one complete
tour.handbook.stage1.step.intro.body:
The tools sit along the edges of the screen: frame and drawing tools together along the top, frame-effect tools along the left, playback controls along the bottom, navigation in the bottom-left corner, settings in the top-right.

Both top toolbars hide extra buttons behind a more button — {icon:cmd:show_more_topmain_tools_toggle} on the top one, {icon:cmd:show_more_topext_tools_toggle} on the left one. This tour walks through the frames your story is built from.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.intro.title: The toolbars
tour.handbook.stage1.step.reorder.body: Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frames_ordering_tool} to unlock reordering. While it is active you can drag frames freely; tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frames_ordering_tool} again to apply the new order, and the story re-forms into a strip.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.reorder.title: {icon:cmd:toggle_frames_ordering_tool} Change the order
tour.handbook.stage1.step.select-frame.b:
Two ways to select a frame:

- tap the frame itself;
- tap its numbered circle in the bottom-left corner.

The selected frame moves to the centre and takes an **orange** outline. The others stay grey.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.strip.body: Tap {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} to arrange every frame into a single strip, centred on screen. This is how you get back to a tidy view after moving things around.
tour.handbook.stage1.step.strip.title: {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} Line the story up
tour.handbook.stage1.title: Stage 1 — Managing frames
tour.handbook.stage2.description: Pencil, eraser, line width and colour — and drawing across several frames.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.colour.body: Pick a colour you like from the strip. Everything you draw from now on uses it.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.colour.title: Change the colour
tour.handbook.stage2.step.done.body:
You have drawn a story. Step by step it becomes simple, if you give yourself a little time and calmly press the right buttons.

Next: playing it back.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.done.title: Stage two complete
tour.handbook.stage2.step.draw-again.bod: Draw the number **2** here. Then do the same in the third frame, and you have a story of three panels.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.draw.body:
Draw the number **1** in the selected frame.

The speed of your hand sets the thickness of the line — move faster for a thicker stroke.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.draw.title: Draw something
tour.handbook.stage2.step.eraser.body: Tap {icon:cmd:editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle} and rub out part of what you drew. Tap {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} again to go back to drawing.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.eraser.title: {icon:cmd:editor_hard_erase_mode_toggle} The eraser
tour.handbook.stage2.step.line-width.bod: The slider on the top toolbar, just under the tool icons, sets stroke thickness. Move it, then draw again to feel the difference.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.next-frame.bod:
Tap the circle numbered **2** in the bottom-left corner. The second frame comes to the centre.

One tap centres a frame; a second tap enlarges it for detailed work.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.pencil.body:
You are already holding it — drawing is the editor's default mode.

{icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} on the top toolbar chooses which SIDE of the canvas you
draw on, rather than turning drawing on and off. Tap it once to move behind your artwork,
and again to come back in front.
tour.handbook.stage2.step.pencil.title: {icon:cmd:editor_draw_mode_toggle} The pencil
tour.handbook.stage2.step.pick-frame.bod: Tap a frame to select it — or tap its numbered circle in the bottom-left corner. The one with the **orange** outline is where your drawing goes.
tour.handbook.stage2.title: Stage 2 — Drawing
tour.handbook.stage3.description: Play, pause, speed, reverse, and stepping frame by frame.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.done.body:
You can not only draw a story now, but control it.

Next — the most interesting part: doing things to the drawings themselves.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.done.title: Stage three complete
tour.handbook.stage3.step.more-tools.bod: Reverse playback lives behind {icon:cmd:show_more_player_tools_toggle}, to the right of the stop button. Tap it to reveal the extra controls.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.pause.body: The same button pauses it while it is playing. Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} again.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.pause.title: {icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} Pause
tour.handbook.stage3.step.play.body: Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} on the bottom toolbar and watch your story run.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.play.title: {icon:cmd:toggle_play_strip_exposition} Play
tour.handbook.stage3.step.reverse.body: Tap {icon:cmd:reverse_strip_exposition}, then play. The story runs in reverse — a different thing to watch than the same story forwards.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.reverse.title: {icon:cmd:reverse_strip_exposition} Play it backwards
tour.handbook.stage3.step.speed.body:
Pick a playback speed: **4×** (fastest), **2×**, **1×**, **0.5×**, **0.25×** (slowest).

Slower is often better for looking at what you drew.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.speed.title: Change the speed
tour.handbook.stage3.step.step-forward.b: {icon:cmd:next_action_strip_exposition} moves the focus one frame on. Keep tapping and it loops around — there is no end to run off.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.stop.body: {icon:cmd:stop_strip_exposition} stops playback. Pressing play afterwards starts again from the beginning, rather than resuming.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.stop.title: {icon:cmd:stop_strip_exposition} Stop
tour.handbook.stage3.step.tidy-up.body: After playback the frames may be scattered. {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} returns them to a strip in the centre of the screen.
tour.handbook.stage3.step.tidy-up.title: {icon:cmd:frames_to_strip_exposition} Back to a strip
tour.handbook.stage3.step.where-it-start:
If a frame has the orange outline, the story plays **from that frame**. To play from the beginning, select frame **1** first.

With nothing selected, the story plays from the start.
tour.handbook.stage3.title: Stage 3 — Playing the story
tour.handbook.stage4.description: Narrative, thermometer, background, and the fire and shatter workspaces.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.back-from-fire: Press the return button when you have finished burning things.
Take your time. Press Next when you want to carry on.
Come back when you are done
tour.handbook.stage4.step.back-from-shat: Play with it for as long as you like. Press the return button to come back to the story, and this tour picks up again.
No hurry — the tour will wait. If you would rather carry on, press Next.
Come back when you are done
tour.handbook.stage4.step.background.bod: Choose a colour in the palette, then tap {icon:cmd:portal_frame_set_aura} on the top toolbar. The frame takes that colour as its background.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.done.body:
You have worked on individual frames of a drawn story — narrative, temperature, colour, and taking an image apart.

That is the whole first level of the app.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.done.title: Stage four complete
tour.handbook.stage4.step.filters.body:
There is one more workspace, opened from the top toolbar, for changing how a drawing looks rather than destroying it: grayscale, blur, hue rotation, colour filters, and folding the image.

Folding is worth knowing about: a folded image **stays folded** when you return to the story. Unfold it in the same workspace where you folded it.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.filters.title: {icon:cmd:gray_scale_filter_value_slider} Colour and composition
tour.handbook.stage4.step.fire.body:
Select a frame and tap {icon:cmd:burn_frame}. Swipe across the drawing and it begins to burn.

Inside that workspace you can shield part of the image from the flames, add fuel so it catches faster, make the flames bigger with the sliders, and put them out with the extinguisher. A restore button brings the image back at any point.
Fire needs gamification switched on: **⚙ Settings → TF-CBT → Enable gamification elements**.

Turn it on and start this tour again to try it, or press Next to carry on without it.
The gamifier controls are not available
tour.handbook.stage4.step.fire.title: {icon:cmd:burn_frame} Fire
tour.handbook.stage4.step.gamifier-panel:
Gamifiers are off until you enable them: **⚙ Settings → TF-CBT → Enable gamification elements**.

With them on, a joystick icon appears in the bottom-right corner and the effect buttons become available on the top toolbar.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.narrative.body:
Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frame_speech_editor} on the top toolbar. The frame moves to the centre and a speech bubble opens beside it.

Type something — «This is number 1» — and press **✓** to apply. The editor also has 🗑️ to clear and **✗** to cancel.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.select-first.b:
Everything in this stage applies to the **selected** frame — the one with the orange outline. The first one is selected already.

To aim these tools at a different frame, tap it, or its numbered circle.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.select-first.t: These tools act on one frame
tour.handbook.stage4.step.shatter.body:
Select a frame and tap {icon:cmd:shatter_frame}. The frame moves into its own workspace.

Tap the drawing anywhere and it shatters like glass. The slider on the left changes how fast, and a restore button brings the image back.
tour.handbook.stage4.step.shatter.fallba:
These effects only appear once gamification is on: **⚙ Settings → TF-CBT → Enable gamification elements**.

Turn it on and start this tour again to try shattering, or press Next to carry on without it.
The gamifier controls are not available
tour.handbook.stage4.step.shatter.title: {icon:cmd:shatter_frame} Shattering
tour.handbook.stage4.step.thermometer.bo:
Tap {icon:cmd:toggle_frame_thermometer}. A scale from 1 to 10 appears at the left edge — drag its slider to set where this frame sits.

The same button removes it again.
tour.handbook.stage4.title: Stage 4 — Frame tools and gamifiers
tour.handbook.stage5.description: Keep a story as a file, and bring it back.
tour.handbook.stage5.step.done.body:
Frames, drawing, playback, per-frame tools, and saving.

You have seen the first level of the app end to end. Everything else builds on these.
tour.handbook.stage5.step.done.title: That is the whole handbook
tour.handbook.stage5.step.restore.body:
1. Tap the **⚙** gear again.
2. **Settings → Storage**.
3. Tap **Upload story from JSON file** and pick your file.

The story loads straight into the workspace.
tour.handbook.stage5.step.restore.title: {icon:cmd:basic_load_json_file} Restoring
tour.handbook.stage5.step.save.body:
1. Tap the **⚙** gear in the top-right corner.
2. In **Settings**, go to **Storage** in the left-hand menu.
3. Tap **Save story to JSON file**.

A short message confirms the file has been downloaded.
tour.handbook.stage5.step.save.title: {icon:cmd:basic_save_json_file} Saving
tour.handbook.stage5.step.warning.body: Loading a story **replaces** what is on screen. If you have unsaved work, save it first.
tour.handbook.stage5.step.warning.title: One thing worth knowing
tour.handbook.stage5.step.why.body: A story can be saved to a file and loaded back later — on this device or another one. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: the file is yours.
tour.handbook.stage5.step.why.title: Your story is a file
tour.handbook.stage5.title: Stage 5 — Saving and restoring
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.description: A few easy moments, each with a simple sign.
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.step.look-t: Parts of your story, side by side.
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.step.mark-e: A sign or a small drawing. Simple is the point here.
Give each one a simple sign
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.step.name-t: If you would like to. Leaving them unnamed is equally fine.
Give any of them a short name
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.step.recall: A place, an activity, a person.
Think of a few pleasant or familiar moments
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.step.slowly: Nothing complicated — just what is easy to recall.
tour.story.enjoy-remembering.title: What I enjoy remembering
tour.story.remains.description: Choosing what to keep, arranging it, and keeping it.
tour.story.remains.step.arrange.body: Order, spacing, grouping — the arrangement is part of what the story says.
tour.story.remains.step.arrange.title: Arrange them however feels right
tour.story.remains.step.choose.body: All of them, or just some. Leaving something out is a choice, not a loss.
tour.story.remains.step.choose.title: Choose the parts you want to keep
tour.story.remains.step.look-back.body: Everything from this session, or from several.
tour.story.remains.step.look-back.title: Look back at what has been created
tour.story.remains.step.preserved.body: You can come back to it any time.
tour.story.remains.step.preserved.title: This story is preserved
tour.story.remains.step.title-it.body: Or leave it unnamed. Both are endings.
tour.story.remains.step.title-it.title: Give the whole story a title
tour.story.remains.title: My story remains
tour.story.small-steps.description: Before, what helped, and after — a story of movement.
tour.story.small-steps.step.after.title: Mark what happened after
tour.story.small-steps.step.before.title: Mark how it was before
tour.story.small-steps.step.recall.body: Even a little. It does not have to be important to anyone else.
tour.story.small-steps.step.recall.title: Think of a moment when something moved forward
tour.story.small-steps.step.the-sequence: This is a story of movement — three marks that go somewhere.
Mark what helped, or what changed
tour.story.small-steps.title: The power of small steps
tour.story.what-happened-today.descripti: Two or three parts of the day, each with its own mark.
tour.story.what-happened-today.step.keep: The day has its own shape now. Keeping it is optional — it existed either way.
Save this, or set it aside
tour.story.what-happened-today.step.look: One sequence, rather than separate pieces.
tour.story.what-happened-today.step.mark: A shape, a colour, a symbol — realistic or abstract, your choice.
tour.story.what-happened-today.step.name: Morning, day, evening — or however it splits for you.
Name two or three parts of today
tour.story.what-happened-today.step.sett: No analysis, no explaining — just noticing.
tour.story.what-happened-today.title: What happened today
tour.story.who-am-i.description: Three to five versions of yourself, each its own shape.
tour.story.who-am-i.step.look-together.b:
Different characters, all part of one story. Take as long as you like here — this is
the part the rest was for.
tour.story.who-am-i.step.mark-each.body: A shape, a character, a colour — realistic or abstract, whatever fits.
tour.story.who-am-i.step.mark-each.title: Give each one a shape
tour.story.who-am-i.step.name-them.body: A short label on any of them. Skipping this is a perfectly good answer.
tour.story.who-am-i.step.name-them.title: Add a word, if you want to
tour.story.who-am-i.step.pick-versions.b: Versions of yourself you recognise — "me, when...". They don't need names yet.
tour.story.who-am-i.step.settle.body:
We're just noticing a few ways you show up. Nothing here is measured, and there is no
wrong shape.
tour.story.who-am-i.step.settle.title: This isn't a test
tour.story.who-am-i.title: Who I am in this day
